annotations.text:
The premise

The last attempt tidied a web dashboard. A tidy dashboard is still a dashboard.

This is a Mac app. One column of type, a quiet sidebar, and almost no chrome. The home screen is three sentences and nothing else — no cards, no counters, no toolbar.

The accent colour appears three times on screen. That is the budget.

Where the buttons went

Nothing is a button until you reach for it. Actions live on the thing they act on, revealed under the pointer — not parked in a toolbar at the other end of the window.

The cost is discoverability, so the first run teaches it once and the sentences stay legible without it.

Recognise, don’t retype

Today the app asks you to type the recipient to confirm — and it sits right above the field, so it gets copied unread.

Three addresses, one is right. A click instead of a line, and it tests the thing that matters: can you tell the real recipient from a planted one.

Benefit before plumbing

The shipped wizard asks for a model provider, a folder path and an IMAP host — before the app has been useful for a single day.

One question instead. What gets configured follows from the answer, and only that.
